releases.notes:
Performance rework for the chunk map, aimed at large explored worlds and low zoom levels, where it was previously close to unusable.

- Terrain no longer gets a unique GPU texture per chunk — chunks now share one texture per 16x16 region, so the map's draw-call count scales with screen area instead of with how small zooming out has made an individual chunk.
- The map's rendered terrain is now mirrored to a small per-region cache file under the world's save folder, so reopening the map shows a picture immediately instead of re-reading and re-decoding every chunk from scratch. Chunk status used for filtering and regen targeting is never taken from this cache — only ever from a read verified in the current session.
- Non-terrain modes (biome, ore density, visited) no longer pay for a terrain read at all, since they never displayed one.
- The chunk grid no longer disappears below zoom level 0 — it thins to wider spacing instead of vanishing.
- At extreme zoom-out, the map groups chunks into small blocks for overlay decisions instead of recomputing every individual chunk's state every frame. Selection and filter-match highlighting no longer scale with how many chunks are on screen at all.

See CHANGELOG.md for details.

**Downloads**: pick the jar matching your Minecraft version and loader.

releases.notes:
First release of Retrograde. **Beta, singleplayer only.**

Retrograde keeps track of which chunks you've actually explored, draws them as a real top-down terrain map, and lets you select chunks on that map and regenerate them — with undo — or hand them to another mod's retrogen.

It doesn't try to work out what's "missing" from a chunk after you add a mod to an existing world. That isn't knowable without re-running world generation. What it does instead is show you where you've been, what's in it, and give you a way to act on a selection of it.

### What's in it

- **A full-screen map**, opened with `O`. Drag or WASD to pan, scroll to zoom toward the cursor. Real terrain drawn with a colour per block, covering everywhere you've explored rather than just the chunks around you — loaded chunks come from memory, the rest straight out of the region files.
- **Four colour modes**: terrain, biome, ore density, and where you've been. The data modes replace the terrain rather than washing over it, so two chunks of the same biome look identical.
- **Per-chunk info** — coordinates, visited or not, biome, and a full scrollable ore tally — in a fixed panel that never covers what you're looking at.
- **Find**, which filters by scope, visited state, slime chunk, biome, and an ore being present or absent, lights the matches up on the map, and selects them nearest-first.
- **Chunk Manipulation** over the still-visible map: regenerate (with a preview, since it's the one action that destroys work), undo from snapshot, another mod's retrogen, and — behind an off-by-default switch — ore and biome editing.
- **Jobs you can get out of.** Everything runs behind a progress screen that moves you clear of the work and puts you back. Cancel is a ladder: stop cleanly, stop now, or let go of a job that's stopped answering. A watchdog on the client tick rescues you if the server thread stops responding.

### Which file do I want?

One jar per Minecraft version and loader:

| Minecraft | Loader | File |
|---|---|---|
| 1.20.1 | Fabric | `retrograde-0.1.0-beta+1.20.1-fabric.jar` |
| 1.20.1 | Forge | `retrograde-0.1.0-beta+1.20.1-forge.jar` |
| 26.1 | Fabric | `retrograde-0.1.0-beta+26.1-fabric.jar` |
| 26.1 | NeoForge | `retrograde-0.1.0-beta+26.1-neoforge.jar` |
| 26.3 | Fabric | `retrograde-0.1.0-beta+26.3-fabric.jar` |
| 26.3 | NeoForge | `retrograde-0.1.0-beta+26.3-neoforge.jar` |

Fabric builds need Fabric API. 1.20.1 pairs with Forge rather than NeoForge because the split didn't happen until 1.20.2.

### Known limitations

- Singleplayer only.
- Find only covers chunks the map has read — chunks that have never generated can't be filtered on.
- Regen is all-or-nothing; it can't keep your builds and redo the terrain around them.
- Mekanism is the only mod-retrogen integration.
- Regen ores has no undo, and can't remove ore.

It's beta because it hasn't been through many hands yet, and because regen rewrites chunks. Back up a world you care about before pointing it at one. Bugs to [Issues](https://github.com/SirStig/Retrograde/issues).
